name: Sequana

attributes.attribute: goddess of the source of the Seine

sources: Green, Miranda. Symbol and Image in Celtic Religious Art. London: Routledge, 1989.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sequana (Sequena) is a Continental Celtic goddess. She gave her name to the river Seine, a boundary between Armorica and the Belgae. Scholars cite the name as a rare Q-Celtic sign in Gaulish. Her cult site sits at the source of the river, at Saint-Germain-Source-Seine. Eight stones there call her dea Sequana. A bronze statuette shows a draped figure with a diadem. She rides a boat whose prow is a swan or a duck, a clear image of the river. The duck held a berry in its beak. While goddesses such as Rhiannon are tied to birds, Sequana alone claims a waterbird as her sign. This drew the cult to healing. People left models of legs, eyes, breasts, and other body parts. The ancient cult continued into Roman rule. The Sequani tribe held the high land between the Aedui and the Helvetii and likely took their name from the river. Her name is a Celtic play on an Old Irish verb for to follow and roll onward.
